summary: A short note from Alex McKenzie at BBN that attaches network traffic statistics for the ARPANET for October 1972. The tables show how many packets each host sent over the period. They cover the whole month, the four days before the ICCC and the three days of the ICCC. BBN had been giving these figures to ARPA each month and now shared them with the whole network community.

plainLanguage.summary: This RFC contains three packet-output tables: the full month of October 1972, four days before the ICCC and the three conference days. Each table separates inter-node from intra-node traffic by host.

questions: how much traffic did each arpanet host send
how many packets did the arpanet carry in 1972
what packet statistics did rfc 413 report
subtitle: October 1972 ARPANET packet statistics, including the ICCC demonstration period.

tldr.problem: The RFC publishes host traffic statistics for October 1972 and separate figures for the days before and during the ICCC.
tldr.mechanism: Three Host Throughput Summary tables report packets output by host, split into inter-node and intra-node traffic.
tldr.outcome: The October table gives totals of 40,711,450 inter-node and 13,589,160 intra-node packets. The unit metadata says the RFC updates RFC 400.

today: The unit metadata lists RFC 413 as Unknown and says it updates RFC 400. It is a historical traffic report for October 1972.

sections.title: Three Reporting Periods
sections.content:
The RFC attaches traffic statistics for the entire month of October 1972, October 20 through 23 before the ICCC, and October 24 through 26 during the ICCC.

The unit metadata says RFC 413 updates RFC 400.
sections.plainLanguage: The report compares three periods: the whole month, the days before the ICCC and the ICCC days. It follows the earlier monthly traffic report.

sections.title: How to Read the Tables
sections.content:
Each table is a Host Throughput Summary of packets output. It lists inter-node packets, intra-node packets, a total, average daily inter-node traffic and the number of days counted. Sites with multiple host entries may also show subtotals.

The full-month table notes missing data for 4 days. TINK and BELV are marked as having no traffic.
sections.plainLanguage: Rows show packet counts for each host, and some sites have several hosts. The full-month table also notes that data is missing for 4 days.

sections.title: Reported Totals
sections.content:
For October, the table reports 40,711,450 inter-node packets and 13,589,160 intra-node packets. It gives daily averages of 1,357,048 inter-node and 452,972 intra-node packets, and a packets-to-messages ratio of 1.07 for internode traffic.

The October 20-23 table reports 8,654,547 inter-node and 1,577,098 intra-node packets. The October 24-26 table reports 8,437,328 inter-node and 895,413 intra-node packets.
sections.plainLanguage: The tables show totals for the month and for each conference period. They make it possible to compare the reported counts without describing why the counts differ.

references.text: RFC 400, the earlier traffic statistics report updated by RFC 413.
